import MatchingLogic.Variable

set_option autoImplicit false

namespace ML
/--
  Given a signature `𝕊 : Type`,
  `Pattern 𝕊` is the type of applicative matching μ-logic patterns over a signature `𝕊`.
  It is defined as a parametrized inductive type.
  The signature `𝕊` can be any type, intended to be read as the "type of symbols".
-/
inductive Pattern (𝕊 : Type) where
| evar : EVar → Pattern 𝕊
| svar : SVar → Pattern 𝕊
| /-- `Pattern.bottom` represents logical falsehood. -/
  bottom : Pattern 𝕊
| /-- `Pattern.symbol σ` is the pattern over signature `𝕊` constructed from a symbol `σ`, where `σ : 𝕊` -/
  symbol : 𝕊 → Pattern 𝕊
| /-- `Pattern.application φ ψ` is the application of `φ` in `ψ` -/
  application : Pattern 𝕊 → Pattern 𝕊 → Pattern 𝕊
| /-- `Pattern.implication φ ψ` is the implication from `φ` to `ψ` -/
  implication : Pattern 𝕊 → Pattern 𝕊 → Pattern 𝕊
| existential : EVar → Pattern 𝕊 → Pattern 𝕊
| mu : SVar → Pattern 𝕊 → Pattern 𝕊
deriving DecidableEq, Inhabited, Repr

namespace Pattern

section NotationsAndAbbreviations

  variable {𝕊 : Type} (φ ψ : Pattern 𝕊)

  /-- Notation for `Pattern.bottom` -/
  notation "⊥" => bottom

  /-- Notation for `Pattern.implication` -/
  infixr:60 (priority := high) " ⇒ " => implication

  /-- Notation for `Pattern.application` -/
  infixl:80 " ⬝ " => application

  /-- Notation for `Pattern.existential -/
  notation "∃∃" => existential

  /-- Notation for `Pattern.mu` -/
  notation "μ " => mu

  /-- Negation of a pattern. -/
  @[match_pattern] def negation := φ ⇒ ⊥
  prefix:70 "∼" => negation

  /-- Disjunction of two patterns. -/
  @[match_pattern] def disjunction := ∼φ ⇒ ψ
  /-- Notation for `Pattern.disjunction -/
  infixl:65 " ⋁ " => disjunction

  /-- Conjunction of two patterns. -/
  @[match_pattern] def conjunction := ∼(∼φ ⋁ ∼ψ)
  /-- Notation for `Pattern.conjunction` -/
  infixl:65 " ⋀ " => conjunction

  /-- The canonical "true" pattern, defined as the negation of `⊥`. -/
  @[match_pattern] def top : Pattern 𝕊 := ∼⊥
  /-- Notation for `Pattern.top` -/
  notation "⊤" => top

  /-- The equivalence (or bidirectional implication) of two patterns. -/
  @[match_pattern] def equivalence := (φ ⇒ ψ) ⋀ (ψ ⇒ φ)
  /-- Notation for `Pattern.equivalence` -/
  infix:50 " ⇔ " => equivalence

  /-- Universal quantification over a pattern. -/
  @[match_pattern] def universal (x : EVar) (φ : Pattern 𝕊) := ∼(∃∃ x (∼φ))
  /-- Notation for `Pattern.universal` -/
  notation "∀∀ " => universal

  instance : Coe EVar (Pattern 𝕊) := ⟨evar⟩

  instance : Coe SVar (Pattern 𝕊) := ⟨svar⟩

end NotationsAndAbbreviations


section Variables

  variable {𝕊 : Type}

  /--
    Returns all the element variables occuring in a pattern, as a list.
    The `x` in `∃∃ x φ` **is not** included
  -/
  @[simp]
  def evars : Pattern 𝕊 → List EVar
  | evar x => [x]
  | svar _ => []
  | ∃∃ _ φ => φ.evars
  | μ _ φ => φ.evars
  | φ ⇒ ψ | φ ⬝ ψ => φ.evars ++ ψ.evars
  | _ => []

  /--
    Returns all the element variables occuring in a pattern, as a list.
    The `x` in `∃∃ x φ` **is** included
  -/
  def allEVars : Pattern 𝕊 → List EVar
  | .evar x => [x]
  | .svar X => []
  | φ ⇒ ψ | φ ⬝ ψ => φ.allEVars ++ ψ.allEVars
  | ∃∃ x φ => x :: φ.allEVars
  | μ X φ => φ.allEVars
  | _ => []

  /-- Answers whether an element variable occurs in a pattern. -/
  @[simp]
  def isEvar (φ : Pattern 𝕊) (x : EVar) : Bool :=
  match φ with
  | evar y => if x = y then true else false
  | ∃∃ _ φ | μ _ φ => φ.isEvar x
  | φ ⬝ ψ | φ ⇒ ψ => φ.isEvar x ∨ ψ.isEvar x
  | _ => false

  theorem evar_equiv_def (φ : Pattern 𝕊) (x : EVar) : x ∈ φ.evars ↔ φ.isEvar x := by
    induction φ with
    | evar y =>
      by_cases h : x = y
      . simp_all
      . simp_all
    | _ => simp [*]

  def countEVar {𝕊} (x : EVar) (φ : Pattern 𝕊) : ℕ :=
    match φ with
    | evar y => if x = y then 1 else 0
    | svar _ => 0
    | ⊥ => 0
    | symbol _ => 0
    | φ ⇒ ψ => φ.countEVar x + ψ.countEVar x
    | φ ⬝ ψ => φ.countEVar x + ψ.countEVar x
    | ∃∃ _ φ => φ.countEVar x
    | μ _ φ => φ.countEVar x

  /-- Returns all element variables occurring free in a pattern, as a list. -/
  @[simp]
  def freeEvars : Pattern 𝕊 → List EVar
  | evar x => [x]
  | svar _ => []
  | ∃∃ x φ => φ.freeEvars.filter (. ≠ x)
  | μ _ φ => φ.freeEvars
  | φ ⇒ ψ | φ ⬝ ψ => φ.freeEvars ++ ψ.freeEvars
  | _ => []

  /-- Answers whether an element variable occurs free in a pattern. -/
  @[simp]
  def isFreeEvar (φ : Pattern 𝕊) (x : EVar) : Bool :=
  match φ with
  | evar y => if x = y then true else false
  | svar _ => false
  | ∃∃ y φ => if x = y then false else φ.isFreeEvar x
  | μ _ φ => φ.isFreeEvar x
  | φ ⇒ ψ | φ ⬝ ψ => φ.isFreeEvar x ∨ ψ.isFreeEvar x
  | _ => false

  theorem free_evar_equiv_def (φ : Pattern 𝕊) (x : EVar) : x ∈ φ.freeEvars ↔ φ.isFreeEvar x := by
    induction φ with
    | evar y =>
      by_cases h : x = y
      . simp_all
      . simp_all
    | existential y φ' ih =>
      apply Iff.intro <;> intros h
      . by_cases h' : x = y <;> simp_all
      . by_cases h' : x = y <;> simp_all
    | _ => simp_all

  theorem evar_of_free_evar {φ : Pattern 𝕊} {x : EVar} : φ.isFreeEvar x → φ.isEvar x := by
    induction φ with
    | existential y φ' ih =>
      by_cases h' : x = y <;> simp_all
    | implication φ₁ φ₂ ih₁ ih₂ | application φ₁ φ₂ ih₁ ih₂ =>
      intro h
      simp only [isFreeEvar, Bool.decide_or, decide_eq_true_eq, Bool.or_eq_true] at h
      simp only [isEvar, Bool.decide_or, decide_eq_true_eq, Bool.or_eq_true]
      exact h.elim (fun h => .inl (ih₁ h)) (fun h => .inr (ih₂ h))
    | _ => simp_all

  @[simp]
  theorem free_var_appl (φ ψ : Pattern 𝕊) (x : EVar) : (φ ⬝ ψ).isFreeEvar x ↔ φ.isFreeEvar x ∨ ψ.isFreeEvar x := by
    simp only [isFreeEvar, Bool.decide_or, Bool.decide_coe, Bool.or_eq_true]

  theorem exists_binds (φ : Pattern 𝕊) (x : EVar) : ¬(∃∃ x φ).isFreeEvar x := by
    simp_all

  @[simp]
  def hasBinderOnEvar (φ : Pattern 𝕊) (x : EVar) : Bool :=
  match φ with
  | ∃∃ y φ => if x = y then true else φ.hasBinderOnEvar x
  | μ _ φ => φ.hasBinderOnEvar x
  | φ ⬝ ψ | φ ⇒ ψ => φ.hasBinderOnEvar x ∨ ψ.hasBinderOnEvar x
  | _ => false

  -- we could also give a recursive definition for this,
  -- but that's a somewhat complicated definition.
  -- TO DECIDE
  @[simp]
  def isBoundEvar (φ : Pattern 𝕊) (x : EVar) : Bool := φ.isEvar x ∧ ¬φ.isFreeEvar x

  instance {φ : Pattern Empty} {x : EVar} : Decidable (isFreeEvar φ x) := inferInstance

  @[simp]
  theorem not_free_evar_exist (φ : Pattern 𝕊) (x : EVar) : ¬(∃∃ x φ).isFreeEvar x := by
    intros h
    induction φ <;> simp at h



  @[simp]
  def svars : Pattern 𝕊 → List SVar
  | evar _ => []
  | svar X => [X]
  | ∃∃ _ φ | μ _ φ => φ.svars
  | φ ⇒ ψ | φ ⬝ ψ => φ.svars ++ ψ.svars
  | _ => []

  def allSVars : Pattern 𝕊 → List SVar
  | .evar x => []
  | .svar X => [X]
  | φ ⇒ ψ | φ ⬝ ψ => φ.allSVars ++ ψ.allSVars
  | ∃∃ x φ => φ.allSVars
  | μ X φ => X :: φ.allSVars
  | _ => []

  @[simp]
  def isSvar (φ : Pattern 𝕊) (X : SVar) : Bool :=
  match φ with
  | svar Y => if X = Y then true else false
  | ∃∃ _ φ | μ _ φ => φ.isSvar X
  | φ ⬝ ψ | φ ⇒ ψ => φ.isSvar X ∨ ψ.isSvar X
  | _ => false



  @[simp]
  def freeSvars : Pattern 𝕊 → List SVar
  | evar _ => []
  | svar X => [X]
  | ∃∃ _ φ => φ.freeSvars
  | μ X φ => φ.freeSvars.filter (. ≠ X)
  | φ ⇒ ψ | φ ⬝ ψ => φ.freeSvars ++ ψ.freeSvars
  | _ => []

  @[simp]
  def isFreeSvar (φ : Pattern 𝕊) (X : SVar) : Bool :=
  match φ with
  | svar Y => if X = Y then true else false
  | evar _ => false
  | μ Y φ => if X = Y then false else φ.isFreeSvar X
  | ∃∃ _ φ => φ.isFreeSvar X
  | φ ⇒ ψ | φ ⬝ ψ => φ.isFreeSvar X ∨ ψ.isFreeSvar X
  | _ => false

  @[simp]
  theorem not_free_svar_mu (φ : Pattern 𝕊) (X : SVar) : ¬(μ X φ).isFreeSvar X := by
    intros h
    induction φ <;> simp at h

  theorem svar_of_free_svar {φ : Pattern 𝕊} {X : SVar} : φ.isFreeSvar X → φ.isSvar X := by
    induction φ with
    | mu Y φ' ih =>
      by_cases h' : X = Y <;> simp_all
    | implication φ₁ φ₂ ih₁ ih₂ | application φ₁ φ₂ ih₁ ih₂ =>
      intro h
      simp only [isFreeSvar, Bool.decide_or, decide_eq_true_eq, Bool.or_eq_true] at h
      simp only [isSvar, Bool.decide_or, decide_eq_true_eq, Bool.or_eq_true]
      exact h.elim (fun h => .inl (ih₁ h)) (fun h => .inr (ih₂ h))
    | _ => simp_all

  @[simp]
  def getFreshEvar : Pattern 𝕊 → EVar
  | φ => .getFresh φ.evars

  -- there are various equivalent definitions of closedness that can be given.
  @[simp]
  def existClosed : Pattern 𝕊 → Prop
  | φ => ∀ x : EVar, ¬φ.isFreeEvar x

  @[simp]
  def muClosed : Pattern 𝕊 → Prop
  | φ => ∀ X : SVar, ¬φ.isFreeSvar X

  /-- Returns the number of `μ`'s present in a pattern. -/
  @[simp]
  def muCount : Pattern 𝕊 → ℕ
  | μ _ φ => φ.muCount + 1
  | φ ⬝ ψ | φ ⇒ ψ => φ.muCount + ψ.muCount
  | ∃∃ _ φ => φ.muCount
  | _ => 0

  /-- Returns the number of `∃`'s present in a pattern. -/
  @[simp]
  def existCount : Pattern 𝕊 → ℕ
  | ∃∃ _ φ => φ.existCount + 1
  | φ ⬝ ψ | φ ⇒ ψ => φ.existCount + ψ.existCount
  | μ _ φ => φ.existCount
  | _ => 0

  /-- Returns the highest number of nested `μ`'s in a pattern. -/
  @[simp]
  def muDepth : Pattern 𝕊 → ℕ
  | μ _ φ => φ.muDepth + 1
  | φ ⬝ ψ | φ ⇒ ψ => max φ.muDepth ψ.muDepth
  | ∃∃ _ φ => φ.muDepth
  | _ => 0

  /-- Returns the highest number of nested `∃`'s in a pattern. -/
  @[simp]
  def existDepth : Pattern 𝕊 → ℕ
  | ∃∃ _ φ => φ.existDepth + 1
  | φ ⬝ ψ | φ ⇒ ψ => max φ.existDepth ψ.existDepth
  | μ _ φ => φ.existDepth
  | _ => 0

end Variables


variable {𝕊 : Type}

@[simp]
def size {𝕊} : Pattern 𝕊 → ℕ
| evar _ | svar _ | ⊥ | symbol _ => 1
| φ ⇒ ψ | φ ⬝ ψ => φ.size + ψ.size + 1
| μ _ φ | ∃∃ _ φ => φ.size + 1

protected def toString [ToString 𝕊] (φ : Pattern 𝕊) : String :=
  match φ with
  | evar x => toString x
  | svar X => toString X
  | ⊥ => "⊥"
  | φ ⇒ ψ => s!"({φ.toString} ⇒ {ψ.toString})"
  | φ ⬝ ψ => s!"({φ.toString} ⬝ {ψ.toString})"
  | ∃∃ x φ => s!"(∃∃{toString x} {φ.toString})"
  | μ X φ => s!"(μ{toString X} {φ.toString})"
  | symbol σ => toString σ

structure Interpretation (𝕊 : Type) (M : Type) where
  evalSymb : 𝕊 → Set M
  evalApp : M → M → Set M

structure Valuation (M : Type) where
  evalEvar : EVar → M
  evalSvar : SVar → Set M

variable {𝕊 : Type} {M : Type}

@[simp]
def Pattern.interpret (I : Interpretation 𝕊 M) (eval : Valuation M) (φ : Pattern 𝕊) : Set M :=
match φ with
| evar x => { eval.evalEvar x }
| svar i => eval.evalSvar i
| symbol σ => I.evalSymb σ
-- TODO (Andrei B): Use set notation?
| φ ⇒ ψ => fun m => (φ.interpret I eval m) → (ψ.interpret I eval m)
| ∃∃ x φ => fun m => ∃ a : M, φ.interpret I ⟨(Function.update eval.evalEvar x a), eval.evalSvar⟩ m
| μ X φ =>
  -- m ∈ ⋂ {B ⊆ M | e(X ← B)⁺ (φ) ⊆ B}
  fun m : M =>
    -- for all B ⊆ M,
    ∀ B : Set M,
      -- if e(X ← B) ⊆ B holds
      (∀ m,
        φ.interpret I ⟨eval.evalEvar, Function.update eval.evalSvar X B⟩ m → B m
      ) →
      -- then m ∈ B
      B m
| p₁ ⬝ p₂ => fun m => ∃ a : M, ∃ b : M, (p₁.interpret I eval a) ∧ (p₂.interpret I eval b) ∧ I.evalApp a b m
| ⊥ => fun _ => False

def muInterpret (I : Interpretation 𝕊 M) (eval : Valuation M) (φ : Pattern 𝕊) (X : SVar) :=
  fun m : M => ∀ B : Set M, φ.interpret I ⟨eval.evalEvar, Function.update eval.evalSvar X B⟩ m → B m

section

  variable {Γ : Premises 𝕊} {φ ψ : Pattern 𝕊} {I : Interpretation 𝕊 M} {e : Valuation M}

  set_option Pattern.pp_interpret_hiding true

  @[simp]
  theorem interpret_bottom : ∀ {m : M}, ⊥.interpret I e m ↔ False := by simp

  @[simp]
  theorem interpret_neg : ∀ {m : M}, (∼φ).interpret I e m ↔ ¬φ.interpret I e m := by
    intros m ; apply Iff.intro <;> (intros h ; simpa)

  @[simp]
  theorem interpret_impl : ∀ {m : M}, (φ ⇒ ψ).interpret I e m ↔ (φ.interpret I e m → ψ.interpret I e m) := by simp

  @[simp]
  theorem interpret_app : ∀ {m : M}, (φ ⬝ ψ).interpret I e m ↔ ∃ a : M, ∃ b : M, (φ.interpret I e a) ∧ (ψ.interpret I e b) ∧ I.evalApp a b m := by simp

  @[simp]
  theorem interpret_disj : ∀ {m : M}, (φ ⋁ ψ).interpret I e m ↔ φ.interpret I e m ∨ ψ.interpret I e m := by
    intros m
    apply Iff.intro <;> intros h
    . simpa
    . rw [or_def_imp_neg] at h
      exact h

  @[simp]
  theorem interpret_exists {x : EVar} : ∀ {m : M}, (∃∃ x φ).interpret I e m ↔ ∃ a : M, φ.interpret I ⟨(Function.update e.evalEvar x a), e.evalSvar⟩ m := by simp

  @[simp]
  theorem implies_false_is_neg { p : Prop } : (p → False) ↔ ¬p := by
    apply Iff.intro <;> intro h <;> intro hp <;> exact h hp

  @[simp]
  theorem equivalence { p q : Prop } : (p → q) ∧ (q → p) ↔ (p ↔ q) := by
    apply Iff.intro <;> intros h
    . cases h with | intro hLeft hRight =>
      apply Iff.intro <;> intros hLocal
      . exact hLeft (hRight (hLeft (hRight (hLeft hLocal))))
      . exact hRight (hLeft (hRight (hLeft (hRight hLocal))))
    . cases h with | intro hLeft hRight =>
      exact And.intro hLeft hRight

  @[simp]
  theorem interpret_equiv: ∀ {m : M}, (φ ⇔ ψ).interpret I e m ↔ (φ.interpret I e m ↔ ψ.interpret I e m) := by
    intros m
    apply Iff.intro <;> intros h
    . simp_all
    . simp_all

  @[simp]
  theorem interpret_conj : ∀ {m : M}, (φ ⋀ ψ).interpret I e m ↔ φ.interpret I e m ∧ ψ.interpret I e m := by
    intro m
    apply Iff.intro <;> intros h
    . simp at h
      assumption
    . simp at *
      assumption

/--
  Typeclass for signatures `𝕊` containing the definedness symbol,
  we name it `defined`.
-/
class HasDefined (𝕊 : Type) where
  defined : 𝕊

/--
  The canonical signature having `definedness` as its only symbol.
-/
inductive Definedness where
| defined

instance : HasDefined Definedness := ⟨Definedness.defined⟩

/-- Notation for `Pattern.symbol HasDefined.defined` -/
notation "⌈" φ "⌉" => (Pattern.symbol HasDefined.defined) ⬝ φ

/--
  The definedness axiom, named simply `definedness`:
  `∀ x. ⌈x⌉`
-/
def definedness {𝕊} [HasDefined 𝕊] {x : EVar} : Pattern 𝕊 := ∀∀ x ⌈.evar x⌉

section variable {𝕊 : Type} [HasDefined 𝕊]

  def total (φ : Pattern 𝕊) : Pattern 𝕊 := ∼⌈∼φ⌉
  notation "⌊" φ "⌋" => total φ

  def equal (φ ψ : Pattern 𝕊) : Pattern 𝕊 := ⌊φ ⇔ ψ⌋
  infix:50 " ≡ "  => equal

  def member (x : EVar) (φ : Pattern 𝕊) : Pattern 𝕊 := ⌈.evar x ⋀ φ⌉
  infix:50 " ∈∈ " => member

  def included (φ ψ : Pattern 𝕊) : Pattern 𝕊 := ⌊φ ⇒ ψ⌋
  infix:50 " ⊆⊆ " => included

end

/--
  A set of premises `Γ` over a signature `𝕊` that contains the
  `defined` symbol satisfies `HasDefinedness` if the definedness axioms belogns to `Γ`.
-/
class HasDefinedness {𝕊} [HasDefined 𝕊] (Γ : Premises 𝕊) where
  hasDefinedness : ∀ {x}, @definedness _ _ x ∈ Γ

/--
  Application context of the form `⌈□⌉`.
-/
def AppContext.CtxDefined {𝕊} [HasDefined 𝕊]: AppContext 𝕊 := .left (Pattern.symbol HasDefined.defined) .empty

  open Lean PrettyPrinter Delaborator SubExpr

  def isApplicationOfDefinedSymbolToPattern : TSyntax `term → Bool
  | `(ML.Pattern.symbol HasDefined.defined)
  | `(ML.Pattern.symbol bdefined)
  | `(Pattern.symbol ML.HasDefined.defined)
  | `(Pattern.symbol HasDefined.defined)
  | `(Pattern.symbol Mdefined)
  | `(symbol ML.HasDefined.defined)

  /--

  -/
  @[delab app.ML.Pattern.application] def delabDefined : Delab := do
    let e ← getExpr
    guard $ e.getAppNumArgs == 3
    let signature ← withAppFn $ withAppFn $ withAppArg $ Delaborator.delab

section Equality
  open Proof
  variable {𝕊 : Type} [HasDefined 𝕊] {Γ : Premises 𝕊} {φ ψ χ : Pattern 𝕊} {C : AppContext 𝕊}

  def equivImplEqual :
    Γ ⊢ φ ⇔ ψ →
    Γ ⊢ (φ ≡ ψ)
    :=
    fun l₁ : Γ ⊢ φ ⇔ ψ =>
    let l₂ : Γ ⊢ ∼⌈∼(φ ⇔ ψ)⌉ := (doubleNegCtx (C := .left _ .empty)) l₁
    let l₃ : Γ ⊢ φ ≡ ψ := l₂
    l₃

  def equalSelf :
    Γ ⊢ φ ≡ φ :=
    let l₁ : Γ ⊢ φ ⇔ φ := equivSelf
    let l₂ : Γ ⊢ φ ≡ φ := (equivImplEqual) l₁
    l₂

  variable [HasDefinedness Γ]

  def definedness' {x : EVar} : Γ ⊢ ⌈.evar x⌉ :=
    let l₁ : Γ ⊢ ∀∀ x ⌈.evar x⌉ := premise (by autopos) HasDefinedness.hasDefinedness
    let l₂ : Γ ⊢ ∀∀ x ⌈.evar x⌉ ⇒ ⌈.evar x⌉.substEvar x (.evar x) := @univQuan _ _ (⌈.evar x⌉) x x (Pattern.substitutable_evar_same _ _)
    let l₃ : Γ ⊢ ∀∀ x ⌈.evar x⌉ ⇒ ⌈.evar x⌉ := by rw [Pattern.subst_var_var_eq_self_evar] at l₂ ; exact l₂
    modusPonens l₁ l₃

end Equality

        intros M _ f _ m
        simp only [Morphism.morphism_impl, Morphism.morphism_disj, Morphism.morphism_conj, Morphism.morphism_neg]
        intros h
        have := Classical.em <| f θ m
        cases this

        . apply Or.inl

          . trivial

  theorem AppContext.not_in_free_evars_insert {x : EVar} : x ∉ φ.evars ++ C.evars → ¬φ.isFreeEvar x ∧ ¬C.isFreeEvar x := by

      rw [←Pattern.free_evar_equiv_def]

      revert this
      rw [←contraposition]
      intros h
      rw [Pattern.free_evar_equiv_def] at h

    .

      revert this
      rw [←contraposition]

      rw [AppContext.evar_equiv_def]

    let l₉ : Γ ⊢ C[x ⋀ φ] ⇒ ⌈φ⌉ := l₈

  def ctxImplDefined : Γ ⊢ C[φ] ⇒ ⌈φ⌉ :=
    let x : EVar := EVar.getFresh (φ.evars ++ C.evars)
    have not_fv_φ : ¬φ.isFreeEvar x := And.left <| AppContext.not_in_free_evars_insert (EVar.get_fresh_is_fresh _)
    have not_fv_C : ¬C.isFreeEvar x := And.right <| AppContext.not_in_free_evars_insert (EVar.get_fresh_is_fresh _)
    let l₉ : Γ ⊢ C[x ⋀ φ] ⇒ ⌈φ⌉ := (ctxImplDefinedAux1) x
    let l₁₀ : Γ ⊢ ∃∃ x (C[x ⋀ φ]) ⇒ ⌈φ⌉ := existGen (by simp_all) l₉
    let l₁₁ : Γ ⊢ φ ⇒ (∃∃ x (x)) ⋀ φ :=
      let l₁' : Γ ⊢ φ ⇒ φ := (implSelf)
      let l₂' : Γ ⊢ ∃∃ x (x) := existence
      let l₃' : Γ ⊢ φ ⇒ ∃∃ x x := (extraPremise) l₂'
      let l₄' : Γ ⊢ φ ⇒ (∃∃ x x) ⋀ φ := (conjIntroRule) l₃' l₁'
      l₄'
    let l₁₂ : Γ ⊢ φ ⇒ ∃∃ x (x ⋀ φ) := (syllogism) l₁₁ ((pushConjInExist) not_fv_φ)
    let l₁₃ : Γ ⊢ C[φ] ⇒ C[(∃∃ x (x ⋀ φ))] := (framing) l₁₂
    let l₁₄ : Γ ⊢ C[(∃∃ x (x ⋀ φ))] ⇒ ⌈φ⌉ :=
      let l₁' : Γ ⊢ C[(∃∃ x (x ⋀ φ))] ⇒ ∃∃ x (C[x ⋀ φ]) := (propagationExist) not_fv_C
      (syllogism) l₁' l₁₀
    let l₁₅ : Γ ⊢ C[φ] ⇒ ⌈φ⌉ := (syllogism) l₁₃ l₁₄
    l₁₅

  def implDefined : Γ ⊢ φ ⇒ ⌈φ⌉ := ctxImplDefined (C := .empty)

  def totalImpl : Γ ⊢ ⌊φ⌋ ⇒ φ :=
    let l₁ : Γ ⊢ ∼φ ⇒ ⌈∼φ⌉ := implDefined
    let l₂ : Γ ⊢ ∼⌈∼φ⌉ ⇒ ∼∼φ := (negImplIntro) l₁
    let l₃ : Γ ⊢ ⌊φ⌋ ⇒ ∼∼φ := l₂
    (syllogism) l₃ (doubleNegElim)

end ContextReasoning

/-
  The AML signature generated from a KORE definition, and the sorted notations
  through which KORE's connectives enter applicative matching logic (AML).

  Every definition here cites the source it transcribes; TRANSLATION.md lists the rules
  with the same rule ids (T-…, S-…, A-…).
  Sources:
  - [Thesis] X. Chen, "Matching mu-Logic", PhD thesis, UIUC 2023:
    §2.13 (printed pp. 29–34), Definition 4.1 (p. 72), §7.2 (pp. 163–165), §7.3.2 (p. 166).
  - [AML-TR] X. Chen, G. Roşu, "Applicative Matching Logic: Semantics of K", TR 2020:
    §4.2 (p. 11), §7 (p. 18), §8 (p. 19), Appendix G.2 (pp. 34–35).
  - [FoSSaCS] X. Chen, H. Cheval, D. Lucanu, G. Roşu, "𝕂 Definitions as Matching Logic
    Theories, Formally", FoSSaCS 2026: §2.3 (pp. 204–206), §4.1 (pp. 208–209).
-/
import MatchingLogic
import KoreParser

set_option autoImplicit false

namespace KoreAML

open ML

/-- The AML signature Σ^AML generated from a KORE definition.

[Thesis] §7.2, p. 163: `Σ^AML = {⌈_⌉, ⊤_} ∪ S^MmL ∪ Σ^MmL`; the constructors below are
that set, extended as TRANSLATION.md records:
`sortSort` (the sort of sorts, [FoSSaCS] §2.3, [AML-TR] §4.2), `ceil` (the MmL definedness
symbols of [Thesis] Def. 2.49, which belong to Σ^MmL), `next` (one-path next, [FoSSaCS] p. 206,
[AML-TR] §8), and the CHOICE constructors `dv`, `str`, `untranslated`. -/
inductive Sym where
  /-- `⌈_⌉`, the AML definedness symbol ([Thesis] (7.7)). -/
  | defined
  /-- `⊤_`, the inhabitant symbol ([Thesis] §7.2); printed `⟦s⟧` as in [AML-TR] §4.2. -/
  | inh
  /-- `Sort`, whose inhabitants are the sorts ([FoSSaCS] §2.3; [Thesis] §7.3.2). -/
  | sortSort
  /-- A KORE sort constructor (`sort` or `hooked-sort`), applied to its sort arguments. -/
  | sort (name : String)
  /-- A KORE symbol (`symbol` or `hooked-symbol`, `inj` included), applied to its sort
  arguments and then to its arguments. -/
  | symbol (name : String)
  /-- The family `⌈_⌉^{s'}_s` of [Thesis] Def. 2.49, applied as `ceil s s' φ`. -/
  | ceil
  /-- `•`, one-path next. -/
  | next
  /-- CHOICE (TRANSLATION.md T-dv): the domain value `\dv{s}("lit")`, applied as `dv_lit s`. -/
  | dv (lit : String)
  /-- CHOICE (TRANSLATION.md T-string): a string-literal pattern; unused by the subject. -/
  | str (lit : String)
  /-- A marker for a construct the translation does not cover (alias applications,
  sorts that cannot be computed); the checks require that none occurs. -/
  | untranslated (what : String)
  deriving DecidableEq, Repr, Inhabited

instance : HasDefined Sym := ⟨Sym.defined⟩

/-- AML patterns over the generated signature. -/
abbrev P := Pattern Sym

def sym (σ : Sym) : P := .symbol σ

/-- `⟦s⟧`, i.e. `⊤_ s`: the inhabitants of sort `s` ([Thesis] §7.2; [AML-TR] §4.2). -/
def inhOf (s : P) : P := sym .inh ⬝ s

/-- `⟦Sort⟧`, the inhabitants of the sort of sorts. -/
def sortsDomain : P := inhOf (sym .sortSort)

/-- Application of a head to a list of arguments, left-nested: `σ φ₁ … φₙ` ([Thesis] (7.14)). -/
def appList (head : P) : List P → P
  | [] => head
  | φ :: φs => appList (head ⬝ φ) φs

/-- Right-nested conjunction, `⊤` when empty: the "well-sorted" conjunction of [Thesis] (7.11). -/
def conjList : List P → P
  | [] => ⊤
  | [φ] => φ
  | φ :: φs => φ ⋀ conjList φs

/-- Right-nested AML disjunction, `⊥` when empty. -/
def disjList : List P → P
  | [] => ⊥
  | [φ] => φ
  | φ :: φs => φ ⋁ disjList φs

/-! ## Sorted connectives

Each is the AML image, under [Thesis] AML2 (7.12)–(7.18), of an MmL primitive or of an MmL
notation ([Thesis] (2.95)–(2.97), (2.100)–(2.103), (4.6)).
The sort arguments `s`, `s'` are AML patterns (sort terms, possibly with sort variables). -/

/-- (7.16): `AML2(¬φ_s) = ¬_s AML2(φ) ≡ ¬AML2(φ) ∧ ⊤_s` (sorted negation). -/
def sNot (s φ : P) : P := (∼φ) ⋀ inhOf s

/-- (7.15): `AML2(φ ∧ φ') = AML2(φ) ∧ AML2(φ')`. -/
def sAnd (φ ψ : P) : P := φ ⋀ ψ

/-- (2.95): `φ₁ ∨ φ₂ ≡ ¬(¬φ₁ ∧ ¬φ₂)`, translated by (7.15), (7.16). -/
def sOr (s φ ψ : P) : P := sNot s (sAnd (sNot s φ) (sNot s ψ))

/-- (2.96): `φ₁ → φ₂ ≡ ¬φ₁ ∨ φ₂`. -/
def sImp (s φ ψ : P) : P := sOr s (sNot s φ) ψ

/-- (2.96): `φ₁ ↔ φ₂ ≡ (φ₁ → φ₂) ∧ (φ₂ → φ₁)`. -/
def sIff (s φ ψ : P) : P := sAnd (sImp s φ ψ) (sImp s ψ φ)

/-- (7.17), with the bound variable's own sort `s'` as [AML-TR] App. G.2 (p. 34) writes it
(the thesis prints `⊤_s`, a typo: see TRANSLATION.md T-exists):
`AML2(∃x:s'. φ) = ∃x. (x ∈ ⊤_{s'}) ∧ AML2(φ)`. -/
def sExists (x : EVar) (s' φ : P) : P := ∃∃ x ((x ∈∈ inhOf s') ⋀ φ)

/-- (2.95): `∀x:s'. φ ≡ ¬∃x:s'. ¬φ`, at the sort `s` of `φ`. -/
def sForall (s : P) (x : EVar) (s' φ : P) : P := sNot s (sExists x s' (sNot s φ))

/-- The element variable bound by `⊤_s ≡ ∃x:s. x:s`.
Index 0 is reserved for it; KORE variables get indices from 1 (see `VarTable`). -/
def topVar : EVar := ⟨0⟩

/-- (2.96): `⊤_s ≡ ∃x:s. x:s`, translated by (7.17), (7.12). -/
def sTop (s : P) : P := sExists topVar s (.evar topVar)

/-- (2.97): `⊥_s ≡ ¬⊤_s`. -/
def sBot (s : P) : P := sNot s (sTop s)

/-- Def. 2.49 (2.98) with (7.14): `AML2(⌈φ⌉^{s'}_s) = ceil s s' AML2(φ)`. -/
def sCeil (s s' φ : P) : P := sym .ceil ⬝ s ⬝ s' ⬝ φ

/-- (2.100): `⌊φ⌋^{s'}_s ≡ ¬⌈¬φ⌉^{s'}_s` (outer negation at `s'`, inner at `s`). -/
def sFloor (s s' φ : P) : P := sNot s' (sCeil s s' (sNot s φ))

/-- (2.101): `φ₁ =^{s'}_s φ₂ ≡ ⌊φ₁ ↔ φ₂⌋^{s'}_s`. -/
def sEquals (s s' φ ψ : P) : P := sFloor s s' (sIff s φ ψ)

/-- (2.102): `x ∈^{s'}_s φ ≡ ⌈x ∧ φ⌉^{s'}_s` (applied to any left operand: TRANSLATION.md T-in). -/
def sIn (s s' φ ψ : P) : P := sCeil s s' (sAnd φ ψ)

/-- `•φ`: one-path next, unsorted as [FoSSaCS] p. 206 and [AML-TR] §8 write it. -/
def sNext (φ : P) : P := sym .next ⬝ φ

/-- `φ → •ψ` at sort `s`: a rewrite rule ([FoSSaCS] p. 206; [AML-TR] §8 (Semantics)). -/
def sRewrites (s φ ψ : P) : P := sImp s φ (sNext ψ)

/-- (4.6): `νX. φ ≡ ¬µX. ¬φ[¬X/X]`, at the sort `s` of `X`, translated by (7.16), (7.18). -/
def sNu (s : P) (X : SVar) (φ : P) : P :=
  sNot s (.mu X (sNot s (φ.substSvar X (sNot s (.svar X)))))

/-! ## Notation for the generated (Γ^AML) axioms -/

/-- `ws ⇒ φ` where `ws` is the conjunction of guards; just `φ` when there is no guard.
Used for the generated axioms (G-rules); translated KORE axioms use (7.10) literally. -/
def guarded : List P → P → P
  | [], φ => φ
  | guards, φ => conjList guards ⇒ φ

/-- The guard of a sort variable `α`: `α ∈ ⟦Sort⟧` (TRANSLATION.md S-param). -/
def sortGuard (α : EVar) : P := α ∈∈ sortsDomain

/-- `φ ≠ ψ`, i.e. `¬(φ = ψ)` ([AML-TR] §2.3; used by [Thesis] (7.8) as `⊤_s ≠ ∅`). -/
def notEqual (φ ψ : P) : P := ∼(φ ≡ ψ)

end KoreAML

/-
  Γ_D's generated parts: Γ_cons's items (constructors, injections, no junk, domain values), the
  closure disjunct of a rule, the denotation of a ground pattern and all-path next. Reviewed
  layer (kept from F0's Curate, Closure and Statements when F0 was removed, P1.4); the core's
  statements (Statements.lean) assemble Γ_D from them.
-/
import KcoreSpec.Kore.Print
import KcoreSpec.Kore.Build

set_option autoImplicit false

namespace KoreAML

open ML

open ML

namespace Cons

/-- The AML sort constant of a sort name (`Nat` ↦ the symbol `SortNat`, as `trSort` gives). -/
def sortP (n : String) : P := sym (.sort ("Sort" ++ n))

def xs (offset n : Nat) : List EVar := (List.range n).map fun i => ⟨offset + i + 1⟩

/-- The pattern a generator of sort `N` builds from argument patterns. -/
def genPat (N : String) : Gen → List P → P
  | .ctor c, args => appList (sym (.symbol c.name)) args
  | .inj A, args => appList (sym (.symbol "inj")) ([sortP A, sortP N] ++ args)

def genName (N : String) : Gen → String
  | .ctor c => Print.unmangle (Print.dropPrefix "Lbl" c.name)
  | .inj A => "inj Sort" ++ A ++ " Sort" ++ N

def memGuards (vs : List EVar) (sorts : List String) : List P :=
  (vs.zip sorts).map fun (x, s) => x ∈∈ inhOf (sortP s)

def names (pre : String) (n : Nat) : List String := (List.range n).map fun i => s!"{pre}{i + 1}"

/-- Cons-Fun: a generator is a total function on its argument sorts,
`x̄ ∈ ⟦s̄⟧ → ∃y:N. g x̄ = y` ([FoSSaCS] §4.1 item 4, p. 208, (Function) form). -/
def funItem (N : String) (g : Gen) : Item :=
  let n := g.argSorts.length
  let x := xs 0 n
  let y : EVar := ⟨n + 1⟩
  { label := s!"cons-fun {genName N g}", rule := "Cons-Fun", names := names "x" n ++ ["y"]
    pat := guarded (memGuards x g.argSorts)
      (sExists y (sortP N) (genPat N g (x.map .evar) ≡ .evar y)) }

/-- Cons-Inj: `g x̄ = g ȳ → x̄ = ȳ` ([FoSSaCS] §4.2 item 1, p. 210). -/
def injItem (N : String) (g : Gen) : Item :=
  let n := g.argSorts.length
  let x := xs 0 n
  let y := xs n n
  { label := s!"cons-inj {genName N g}", rule := "Cons-Inj", names := names "x" n ++ names "y" n
    pat := guarded (memGuards x g.argSorts ++ memGuards y g.argSorts)
      ((genPat N g (x.map .evar) ≡ genPat N g (y.map .evar)) ⇒
        conjList ((x.zip y).map fun (a, b) => .evar a ≡ .evar b)) }

/-- Cons-Dist: `g x̄ ≠ g' ȳ` for two generators of one sort ([FoSSaCS] §4.2 item 2, p. 210). -/
def distItem (N : String) (g g' : Gen) : Item :=
  let n := g.argSorts.length
  let m := g'.argSorts.length
  let x := xs 0 n
  let y := xs n m
  { label := s!"cons-dist {genName N g} / {genName N g'}", rule := "Cons-Dist"
    names := names "x" n ++ names "y" m
    pat := guarded (memGuards x g.argSorts ++ memGuards y g'.argSorts)
      (notEqual (genPat N g (x.map .evar)) (genPat N g' (y.map .evar))) }

/-- Cons-Coh: `inj{B,C}(inj{A,B}(x)) = inj{A,C}(x)` for a chain `A < B < C`
([AML-TR] §6, pp. 16–17: the triangle that coercions must satisfy). -/
def cohItem (A B C : String) : Item :=
  let x : EVar := ⟨1⟩
  let inj := fun (s t : String) (φ : P) => appList (sym (.symbol "inj")) [sortP s, sortP t, φ]
  { label := s!"cons-coh Sort{A} < Sort{B} < Sort{C}", rule := "Cons-Coh", names := ["x"]
    pat := guarded [x ∈∈ inhOf (sortP A)] (inj B C (inj A B (.evar x)) ≡ inj A C (.evar x)) }

/-- Cons-NoJunk: `⟦N⟧ = μX. ⋁_g g Ȳ`, `Yⱼ = X` where g's j-th argument sort is N, `⟦sⱼ⟧` otherwise
([FoSSaCS] §4.2 item 3, p. 210; [AML-TR] App. F, Proposition 24); an injection `inj{A,N}`
contributes `inj A N ⟦A⟧`, the KORE form of the paper's subsort disjunct `⊤_A`. -/
def noJunkItem (N : String) (gs : List Gen) : Item :=
  let X : SVar := ⟨1⟩
  let arg := fun (s : String) => if s == N then .svar X else inhOf (sortP s)
  { label := s!"cons-nojunk Sort{N}", rule := "Cons-NoJunk", names := ["X"]
    pat := inhOf (sortP N) ≡ .mu X (disjList (gs.map fun g => genPat N g (g.argSorts.map arg))) }

end Cons

/-- `s ∈ ⟦Sort⟧ → ∃y:s. dv"v" s = y`: the domain value `\dv{s}("v")` denotes one element.
NOT part of Γ_D (decision D1 keeps T-dv's arity-only reading for milestone 1); it is assumed only
where STATEMENTS.md asks for a model in which ground configurations denote single elements. -/
def dvFunItem (lit : String) : Item :=
  let s : EVar := ⟨1⟩
  let y : EVar := ⟨2⟩
  { label := s!"dv-fun \"{lit}\"", rule := "DV-Fun", names := ["s", "y"]
    pat := guarded [sortGuard s] (sExists y (.evar s) (sym (.dv lit) ⬝ .evar s ≡ .evar y)) }

def dvFunctional : Premises Sym := fun φ => ∃ lit : String, φ = (dvFunItem lit).pat

/-- The premises a list of items denotes, with aml-port's `definedness` at every variable
(as `Theory.premises`). -/
def itemsPremises (its : List Item) : Premises Sym :=
  fun φ => (∃ it ∈ its, it.pat = φ) ∨ ∃ x : EVar, φ = @definedness Sym _ x

/-- G-dv-arity for every literal string: `s ∈ ⟦Sort⟧ → dv"v" s ⊆ ⟦s⟧`, an infinite schema.
The encoding (`Theory.ofDefinition`) lists the instances for the literals occurring in D; ground
configurations may contain any literal (`\dv{SortInt{}}("5")`), and without its arity axiom such a
literal could denote elements outside its sort (review finding 1). Arity only: no functionality,
no distinctness (decision D1). -/
def dvArityAll : Premises Sym := fun φ => ∃ lit : String, φ = (dvArityItem lit).pat

open ML

/-- One rule's disjunct, `∃x̄:s̄. (L ∧ y ∈ R)`, for the rule axiom `\rewrites{C}(L, R)`, with the
rule's variables numbered from `offset + 1` (so that the disjuncts of different rules use disjoint
indices), and the names of those variables. -/
def closureDisjunct (aliases : List String) (offset : Nat) (y : EVar) (pat : Kore.Pattern) :
    List String × P :=
  let t0 := tableOf [] pat
  let table : VarTable := List.replicate offset (.sortVar "#pad") ++ t0
  let c : Ctx := ⟨table, aliases⟩
  let (L, R) := match pat with
    | .rewrites _ l r => (tr c l, tr c r)
    | _ => (⊥, ⊥)
  let free := (freeOf [] pat).eraseDups.filterMap fun
    | k@(.evar _ s) => some (k, s)
    | _ => none
  (t0.map VarKey.name,
   free.foldr (fun (k, s) φ => sExists (table.ev k) (trSort table s) φ) (L ⋀ (y ∈∈ R)))

open ML

/-- ⟦t⟧: the AML pattern of a ground term, by the translation (T-app, T-dv). It has no free
variable, so its interpretation does not depend on the valuation. -/
def den (t : Kore.Pattern) : P := tr ⟨[], []⟩ t

/-- The valuation used to read closed patterns. -/
def val0 {M : Type} [Inhabited M] : Valuation M := ⟨fun _ => default, fun _ _ => False⟩

/-- `◦φ ≡ ¬•¬φ`, all-path next (OOPSLA 2023 p. 13): every successor matches φ.
`◦⊥` is `¬•⊤`: no successor. -/
def allNext (φ : P) : P := ∼(sNext (∼φ))

end KoreAML

/-
  KCore. The matching-logic theory of a semantics, built from `Semantics` alone, and the
  statements that the step relation is faithful to it.

  `Γ c` reads the kernel's data and its interpretation of the parameter symbols (`c.hooks`); it
  reads no presentation and no KORE text. It is the union of six parts, each a definition of its
  own:
  - `ΓSig`: the axioms of the encoding (definedness, the sorts, the arity of every symbol, the
    definedness symbols, next, domain values);
  - `ΓCons`: the constructor sorts' axioms (`consItemsK`, the collection sorts left out);
  - `ΓDomains`: the graphs of the interpreted and parameter symbols, that every value is one
    element, distinctness of values, no junk in each collection sort;
  - `ΓColls`: what each collection sort's unit, element and concatenation are on any elements of
    their sorts (a union of maps, a concatenation of lists);
  - `ΓFns`: each function's equations, one per clause with the clauses of a smaller priority
    negated, and its closure axiom;
  - `ΓRules`: each rule's axiom, the rules of a smaller priority negated.
  `Γstep c` is the step's closure axiom.

  Variables of clauses and rules are named canonically (`V0`, `V1`, …): a name only fixes an
  index of the translation. Every axiom is translated by `trAxiom` with no declarations and no
  aliases: it reads declarations only for the sort of an application at the top of an axiom, and
  aliases only at an alias application; no axiom here has either.

  `StepSound`, `StepComplete` and `HasModel` state what the theory is for; `Hyp` is what they
  assume. They are statements only.
-/
import KcoreSpec.Statements
import KcoreSpec.SubjectReduction

set_option autoImplicit false

namespace KCore

namespace Faithful

open ML
open KoreAML (R)

/-! ## Canonical variables -/

/-- `V0, V1, …, V(n-1)`. -/
def canonNames (n : Nat) : List String := (List.range n).map fun i => "V" ++ toString i

/-- The variables of a clause or rule of sorts `sorts`, named canonically. -/
def canonVars (c : Semantics) (sorts : List Srt) : List KoreAML.Var :=
  KoreAML.varList (sorts.map c.sortName) (canonNames sorts.length)

/-- A rule's variable names, canonical; nothing else of a rule's presentation is read here. -/
def canonRulePres (r : Rule) : RulePres :=
  { (default : RulePres) with names := canonNames r.vars.length }

/-- A clause's variable names, canonical, the same names for its exclusion (an exclusion binds its
variables, so it may reuse the names of the equation it occurs in). -/
def canonClausePres (cl : Clause) : ClausePres :=
  { (default : ClausePres) with names := canonNames cl.vars.length, exclNames := canonNames cl.vars.length }

/-- A function's variable names, canonical. -/
def canonFnPres (f : Fn) : FnPres :=
  { (default : FnPres) with clauses := f.clauses.map canonClausePres }

/-- The items of the axioms among `ss`, each translated by `trAxiom` with no declarations and no
aliases. -/
def kernelItems (ss : List Kore.Sentence) : List KoreAML.Item :=
  ss.filterMap fun
    | .axiom a => some (KoreAML.trAxiom [] [] ⟨0, "kernel", a⟩)
    | _ => none

/-- An application of `f` as `Term.kore` writes it: `Lblite{SortX}(…)` for a symbol named
`ite{X}`, `f(…)` with no sort argument otherwise. The registry's `kIte` is named `Lblite`, with no
sort in its name, so `Term.kore` applies it, if at all, as the sortless `Lblite(…)` written here;
a definition applies `ite` at a sort through its own parameter symbol `ite{X}`. -/
def symApp (c : Semantics) (f : Sym) (args : List Kore.Pattern) : Kore.Pattern :=
  match iteSort? (c.symName f) with
  | some X => .app ⟨⟨"Lblite"⟩⟩ [KoreAML.srt X] args
  | none => .app ⟨⟨c.symName f⟩⟩ [] args

/-! ## 1. The signature -/

/-- A sort as a declaration without parameters, under its KORE name `SortX`. -/
def sortDeclOf (c : Semantics) (s : Srt) : KoreAML.SortDecl := ⟨"Sort" ++ c.sortName s, [], false⟩

/-- G-arity of a symbol, `f ⟦s₁⟧ … ⟦sₙ⟧ ⊆ ⟦s⟧`, at the head `Term.kore` applies: `arityItem` of
its declaration for an ordinary symbol; for a symbol named `ite{X}`, the same inclusion with the
head `Lblite` applied to the sort `SortX`, which is how the translation of a term applies it. -/
def symArityItem (c : Semantics) (k : CtorSig) : KoreAML.Item :=
  match iteSort? (c.symName k.name) with
  | none => KoreAML.arityItem ⟨c.symName k.name, [], k.args.map (srtOf c), srtOf c k.result, false, []⟩
  | some X =>
    { label := "arity Lblite at Sort" ++ X, rule := "G-arity", names := []
      pat := KoreAML.appList (KoreAML.sym (.symbol "Lblite") ⬝ sortP X)
          (k.args.map fun s => KoreAML.inhOf (sortP (c.sortName s))) ⊆⊆
        KoreAML.inhOf (sortP (c.sortName k.result)) }

/-- The signature's items: definedness; per sort, that its name denotes one sort (G-sort); per
symbol, its arity; the arity and definedness of the definedness symbols; the arity of next at the
configuration sort.

No sort is said to be inhabited (G-nonempty). A sort is interpreted by its values, and some
numbered sorts have none (Float: `dvOK` admits no Float literal and no constructor builds one);
G-nonempty would put an element in such a sort, at which the equations of a function on a
supersort are read although the function is evaluated at values only. A sort that has a value is
inhabited without it: the value denotes an element of the sort (`ΓDomains`). -/
def sigItems (c : Semantics) : List KoreAML.Item :=
  [KoreAML.definednessItem] ++
  (kernelSorts c).map (fun s => KoreAML.sortConstantItem (sortDeclOf c s)) ++
  (kernelSyms c).map (symArityItem c) ++
  [KoreAML.ceilArityItem, KoreAML.ceilDefItem, KoreAML.nextArityItem [] (srtOf c topCellSort)]

/-- **The signature.** The axioms that make the encoding of sorted matching logic in applicative
matching logic mean what it should: `⌈_⌉` is definedness, each sort is a sort,
each symbol maps arguments of its argument sorts into its result sort, `⌈_⌉{s,s'}` behaves as
definedness, next keeps a configuration a configuration, and a domain value of any literal lies in
its sort (`dvArityAll`, for every literal, since a ground value may carry any). These are the items
`Theory.ofDefinition` builds from a text's declarations, built from the semantics' lists of sorts
and symbols instead, less G-nonempty (`sigItems`). -/
def ΓSig (c : Semantics) : Premises KoreAML.Sym := fun φ =>
  KoreAML.itemsPremises (sigItems c) φ ∨ KoreAML.dvArityAll φ

/-! ## 2. The constructors -/

/-- The constructors' items, over `consSorts`: per sort, each generator's functionality and
injectivity, the distinctness of each pair (Cons-Dist for constructors and for injections without a
common lower bound, Cons-Dist′ with one, `distLbItem`; none for comparable injections), and
no-junk; then the coherence triangles of every chain of `subsorts` (which holds the closure of the
declared pairs). -/
def consItemsK (c : Semantics) : List KoreAML.Item :=
  let n := c.sortName
  let perSort := (consSorts c).flatMap fun N =>
    let gs := c.gens N
    (gs.map (Gen.toK c)).map (KoreAML.Cons.funItem (n N)) ++
    ((gs.map (Gen.toK c)).filter (!·.argSorts.isEmpty)).map (KoreAML.Cons.injItem (n N)) ++
    (pairs gs).flatMap (fun (g, g') => match g, g' with
      | .inj a, .inj b =>
        if c.le a b || c.le b a then []
        else match c.lowerBounds a b with
          | [] => [KoreAML.Cons.distItem (n N) (Gen.toK c g) (Gen.toK c g')]
          | lbs => [distLbItem (n N) (n a) (n b) (lbs.map n)]
      | _, _ => [KoreAML.Cons.distItem (n N) (Gen.toK c g) (Gen.toK c g')]) ++
    [KoreAML.Cons.noJunkItem (n N) (gs.map (Gen.toK c))]
  let coh := c.subsorts.flatMap fun (a, b) =>
    (c.subsorts.filter (·.1 == b)).map fun (_, e) => KoreAML.Cons.cohItem (n a) (n b) (n e)
  perSort ++ coh

/-- **The constructors.** Per constructor sort, each generator is a total function, injective, and
apart from the others, and the sort holds nothing but what its generators build; injections
compose along every chain of subsorts.

The definition's own collection sorts are left out of the sorts it ranges over. The elements of a collection sort are not built by constructors: its unit, element
and concatenation symbols are parameter symbols, so its only generators are injections from its
subsorts, and a no-junk item over those would exclude the empty collection and every collection
of two or more elements. Its elements are pinned by the domains instead: every value is one
element, distinct values are distinct, and `collNoJunk`. -/
def ΓCons (c : Semantics) : Premises KoreAML.Sym := KoreAML.itemsPremises (consItemsK c)

/-! ## 3. The domains -/

/-- No junk in the collection sort of `k`: `⟦S⟧ ⊆ μX. unit ∨ concat(elem(⟦K⟧, ⟦V⟧), X)` for a map,
`⟦S⟧ ⊆ μX. unit ∨ concat(elem(⟦K⟧), X)` for a set or a list, with `k`'s symbols and sorts. Every
element of the sort is built from its unit by adding elements one at a time. -/
def collNoJunk (c : Semantics) (k : CollSig) : KoreAML.P :=
  let X : SVar := ⟨1⟩
  let el := match k.kind with
    | .map => KoreAML.appList (symP (c.symName k.elem))
        [KoreAML.inhOf (sortP (c.sortName k.key)), KoreAML.inhOf (sortP (c.sortName (valSort k)))]
    | _ => KoreAML.appList (symP (c.symName k.elem)) [KoreAML.inhOf (sortP (c.sortName k.key))]
  KoreAML.inhOf (sortP (c.sortName k.sort)) ⊆⊆
    .mu X (symP (c.symName k.unit) ⋁ KoreAML.appList (symP (c.symName k.concat)) [el, .svar X])

/-- **The domains.** What the semantics says of its values and of the symbols it interprets:
- the graph of every interpreted hooked symbol on ground values of its argument sorts, ⊥ where it
  is undefined; the graph of every parameter symbol under the semantics' interpretation of its
  parameters (`paramVal`, which reads `c.hooks`), ⊥ where that is undefined; each written as the
  translation of a term writes the application (`symApp`), so the graph of `ite` at a sort is
  about `Lblite` applied to that sort;
- every ground value of a sort denotes exactly one element of that sort, `∃y:s. ⟦v⟧ = y`;
- distinct values of one sort among `distinctSorts` denote distinct elements;
- no junk in each collection sort (`collNoJunk`).

That a value is an element follows from the constructors' functionality for a constructor term;
for a collection nothing else gives it. -/
def ΓDomains (c : Semantics) : Premises KoreAML.Sym := fun φ =>
  (∃ (k : CtorSig) (vs : List GroundTerm) (r : Option GroundTerm),
      k ∈ hookSigs ∧ c.sortsOf vs = some k.args ∧ hook k.name vs = some r ∧
      φ = (KoreAML.den (symApp c k.name (GroundTerm.koreList c vs)) ≡ (match r with
        | some v => den c v
        | none => ⊥))) ∨
  (∃ (k : ParamSig) (vs : List GroundTerm),
      k ∈ c.params ∧ c.sortsOf vs = some k.sig.args ∧
      φ = (KoreAML.den (symApp c k.sig.name (GroundTerm.koreList c vs)) ≡
        (match c.paramVal k.sig.name vs with
          | some v => den c v
          | none => ⊥))) ∨
  (∃ (v : GroundTerm) (s : Srt), c.sortOf v = some s ∧
      φ = KoreAML.sExists ⟨1⟩ (sortP (c.sortName s)) (den c v ≡ .evar ⟨1⟩)) ∨
  (∃ (v w : GroundTerm) (s : Srt),
      (distinctSorts c).contains s = true ∧
      c.sortOf v = some s ∧ c.sortOf w = some s ∧ GroundTerm.cmp v w ≠ .eq ∧
      φ = ∼(den c v ⋀ den c w)) ∨
  (∃ k ∈ c.allColls, φ = collNoJunk c k)

/-! ## 4. The collections

The axioms that say what a collection sort's unit, element and concatenation symbols are on
elements that need not be values' elements. `ΓDomains` gives their graphs on values only; a
negated premise reads a collection pattern at any elements of its sorts (FaithfulColl.lean has a
model of the other parts in which a map pattern holds of a map it does not match). Each axiom is
true of the intended model: a map sort's elements are the finite maps from its key sort's
elements to its value sort's, `elem(a, b)` the map of one entry `a ↦ b`, the unit the empty map,
`concat` the union of two maps with disjoint keys and nothing (`∅`) where their keys overlap; a
list sort's elements are the finite sequences of its element sort's elements, `elem(a)` the
sequence `[a]`, the unit `[]`, `concat` concatenation (total). A set sort gets none: the only set
pattern a left-hand side holds is the unit (`collPatternHooks`), which the graphs read. -/

section
variable (c : Semantics) (k : CollSig)

/-- The unit of the collection `k`, as the KORE of a value writes it. -/
def collU : KoreAML.P := symP (c.symName k.unit)
/-- `elem(a, b)`: an entry of the map collection `k`. -/
def collE (a b : KoreAML.P) : KoreAML.P := KoreAML.appList (symP (c.symName k.elem)) [a, b]
/-- `concat(a, b)` in the collection `k`. -/
def collC (a b : KoreAML.P) : KoreAML.P := KoreAML.appList (symP (c.symName k.concat)) [a, b]
/-- The inhabitants of the sort `s`. -/
def inSort (s : Srt) : KoreAML.P := KoreAML.inhOf (sortP (c.sortName s))

/-- **A map's unit is a union of units only.** `∀ m₁ m₂ : S. ⌈unit ∧ concat(m₁, m₂)⌉ → m₁ = unit ∧
m₂ = unit`. True of finite maps: if `m₁ ∪ m₂` is defined and empty, both have no key, so both are
the empty map. -/
def mapUnitSplitAx : KoreAML.P :=
  let m₁ : EVar := ⟨1⟩
  let m₂ : EVar := ⟨2⟩
  KoreAML.guarded [m₁ ∈∈ inSort c k.sort, m₂ ∈∈ inSort c k.sort]
    (⌈collU c k ⋀ collC c k (.evar m₁) (.evar m₂)⌉ ⇒ ((.evar m₁ ≡ collU c k) ⋀ (.evar m₂ ≡ collU c k)))

/-- **An entry is not the unit.** `∀ a : K, b : V. ¬⌈unit ∧ elem(a, b)⌉`. True of finite maps:
`a ↦ b` has the key `a`, the empty map has none. -/
def mapElemNotUnitAx : KoreAML.P :=
  let a : EVar := ⟨1⟩
  let b : EVar := ⟨2⟩
  KoreAML.guarded [a ∈∈ inSort c k.key, b ∈∈ inSort c (valSort k)]
    (∼⌈collU c k ⋀ collE c k (.evar a) (.evar b)⌉)

/-- **An entry is atomic.** `∀ a a' : K, b b' : V, r : S.
⌈elem(a', b') ∧ concat(elem(a, b), r)⌉ → a = a' ∧ b = b' ∧ r = unit`. True of finite maps: if
`{a' ↦ b'} = {a ↦ b} ∪ r` with disjoint keys, the union has the key `a` with the value `b`, so
`a = a'` and `b = b'`, and `r` has no key besides `a`, which it does not have, so `r` is empty. -/
def mapElemAtomAx : KoreAML.P :=
  let a : EVar := ⟨1⟩
  let b : EVar := ⟨2⟩
  let a' : EVar := ⟨3⟩
  let b' : EVar := ⟨4⟩
  let r : EVar := ⟨5⟩
  KoreAML.guarded [a ∈∈ inSort c k.key, b ∈∈ inSort c (valSort k), a' ∈∈ inSort c k.key, b' ∈∈ inSort c (valSort k),
      r ∈∈ inSort c k.sort]
    (⌈collE c k (.evar a') (.evar b') ⋀ collC c k (collE c k (.evar a) (.evar b)) (.evar r)⌉ ⇒
      ((.evar a ≡ .evar a') ⋀ (.evar b ≡ .evar b') ⋀ (.evar r ≡ collU c k)))

/-- **An entry of a union is an entry of one part.** `∀ a : K, b : V, r m₁ m₂ : S.
⌈concat(elem(a, b), r) ∧ concat(m₁, m₂)⌉ → (∃y:S. m₁ = concat(elem(a, b), y) ∧ r = concat(y, m₂)) ∨
(∃y:S. m₂ = concat(elem(a, b), y) ∧ r = concat(m₁, y))`. True of finite maps: let
`M = {a ↦ b} ∪ r = m₁ ∪ m₂`, both unions defined. `M` has the key `a`, so one part has it, say
`m₁`, with the value `M(a) = b`; take `y = m₁` without `a`. Then `m₁ = {a ↦ b} ∪ y` (defined: `y`
lacks `a`), and `y ∪ m₂` is defined (`y ⊆ m₁`, whose keys are apart from `m₂`'s) and is `M`
without `a`, which is `r` (`r` lacks `a`, and `M = {a ↦ b} ∪ r`). Symmetrically when `m₂` has
`a`. -/
def mapDecompAx : KoreAML.P :=
  let a : EVar := ⟨1⟩
  let b : EVar := ⟨2⟩
  let r : EVar := ⟨3⟩
  let m₁ : EVar := ⟨4⟩
  let m₂ : EVar := ⟨5⟩
  let y : EVar := ⟨6⟩
  let ab := collE c k (.evar a) (.evar b)
  KoreAML.guarded [a ∈∈ inSort c k.key, b ∈∈ inSort c (valSort k), r ∈∈ inSort c k.sort, m₁ ∈∈ inSort c k.sort,
      m₂ ∈∈ inSort c k.sort]
    (⌈collC c k ab (.evar r) ⋀ collC c k (.evar m₁) (.evar m₂)⌉ ⇒
      (KoreAML.sExists y (sortP (c.sortName k.sort))
          ((.evar m₁ ≡ collC c k ab (.evar y)) ⋀ (.evar r ≡ collC c k (.evar y) (.evar m₂))) ⋁
        KoreAML.sExists y (sortP (c.sortName k.sort))
          ((.evar m₂ ≡ collC c k ab (.evar y)) ⋀ (.evar r ≡ collC c k (.evar m₁) (.evar y)))))

/-- The axioms of a map collection. -/
def mapCollAxioms : List KoreAML.P :=
  [mapUnitSplitAx c k, mapElemNotUnitAx c k, mapElemAtomAx c k, mapDecompAx c k]

/-- `elem(a)`: an item of the list collection `k`. -/
def collI (a : KoreAML.P) : KoreAML.P := KoreAML.appList (symP (c.symName k.elem)) [a]

/-- **A list's unit is a concatenation of units only.** `∀ l₁ l₂ : S. ⌈unit ∧ concat(l₁, l₂)⌉ →
l₁ = unit ∧ l₂ = unit`. True of finite sequences: `l₁ ++ l₂ = []` has length `|l₁| + |l₂| = 0`, so
both are empty. -/
def listUnitSplitAx : KoreAML.P :=
  let l₁ : EVar := ⟨1⟩
  let l₂ : EVar := ⟨2⟩
  KoreAML.guarded [l₁ ∈∈ inSort c k.sort, l₂ ∈∈ inSort c k.sort]
    (⌈collU c k ⋀ collC c k (.evar l₁) (.evar l₂)⌉ ⇒ ((.evar l₁ ≡ collU c k) ⋀ (.evar l₂ ≡ collU c k)))

/-- **An item is not the unit.** `∀ a : K. ¬⌈unit ∧ elem(a)⌉`. True of finite sequences: `[a]` has
length one, `[]` length zero. -/
def listElemNotUnitAx : KoreAML.P :=
  let a : EVar := ⟨1⟩
  KoreAML.guarded [a ∈∈ inSort c k.key] (∼⌈collU c k ⋀ collI c k (.evar a)⌉)

/-- **An item is atomic, from the front.** `∀ a a' : K, r : S. ⌈elem(a') ∧ concat(elem(a), r)⌉ →
a = a' ∧ r = unit`. True of finite sequences: if `[a'] = a :: r`, the heads are equal and the
tail `r` is the tail of `[a']`, which is empty. -/
def listElemAtomAx : KoreAML.P :=
  let a : EVar := ⟨1⟩
  let a' : EVar := ⟨2⟩
  let r : EVar := ⟨3⟩
  KoreAML.guarded [a ∈∈ inSort c k.key, a' ∈∈ inSort c k.key, r ∈∈ inSort c k.sort]
    (⌈collI c k (.evar a') ⋀ collC c k (collI c k (.evar a)) (.evar r)⌉ ⇒
      ((.evar a ≡ .evar a') ⋀ (.evar r ≡ collU c k)))

/-- **An item is atomic, from the back.** `∀ a a' : K, r : S. ⌈elem(a') ∧ concat(r, elem(a))⌉ →
a = a' ∧ r = unit`. True of finite sequences: if `[a'] = r ++ [a]`, the lengths give `|r| = 0`, so
`r` is empty and `[a'] = [a]`. -/
def listElemAtomBackAx : KoreAML.P :=
  let a : EVar := ⟨1⟩
  let a' : EVar := ⟨2⟩
  let r : EVar := ⟨3⟩
  KoreAML.guarded [a ∈∈ inSort c k.key, a' ∈∈ inSort c k.key, r ∈∈ inSort c k.sort]
    (⌈collI c k (.evar a') ⋀ collC c k (.evar r) (collI c k (.evar a))⌉ ⇒
      ((.evar a ≡ .evar a') ⋀ (.evar r ≡ collU c k)))

/-- **A concatenation's first item is the first part's, or the second's when the first is empty.**
`∀ a : K, r l₁ l₂ : S. ⌈concat(elem(a), r) ∧ concat(l₁, l₂)⌉ →
(l₁ = unit ∧ l₂ = concat(elem(a), r)) ∨ (∃y:S. l₁ = concat(elem(a), y) ∧ r = concat(y, l₂))`. True
of finite sequences: let `a :: r = l₁ ++ l₂`. If `l₁` is empty, `l₂ = a :: r`. Otherwise `l₁` has
a head, which is the head `a` of `l₁ ++ l₂`; take `y` its tail, so `l₁ = a :: y`, and the tails of
`a :: r = a :: (y ++ l₂)` are equal, `r = y ++ l₂`. A value is decomposed from its first item, so
this front form is the one that splits a value's element along any concatenation; a pattern that
takes an item from the back (`L ListItem(_)`) is a concatenation like any other. -/
def listDecompAx : KoreAML.P :=
  let a : EVar := ⟨1⟩
  let r : EVar := ⟨2⟩
  let l₁ : EVar := ⟨3⟩
  let l₂ : EVar := ⟨4⟩
  let y : EVar := ⟨5⟩
  let ia := collI c k (.evar a)
  KoreAML.guarded [a ∈∈ inSort c k.key, r ∈∈ inSort c k.sort, l₁ ∈∈ inSort c k.sort, l₂ ∈∈ inSort c k.sort]
    (⌈collC c k ia (.evar r) ⋀ collC c k (.evar l₁) (.evar l₂)⌉ ⇒
      (((.evar l₁ ≡ collU c k) ⋀ (.evar l₂ ≡ collC c k ia (.evar r))) ⋁
        KoreAML.sExists y (sortP (c.sortName k.sort))
          ((.evar l₁ ≡ collC c k ia (.evar y)) ⋀ (.evar r ≡ collC c k (.evar y) (.evar l₂)))))

/-- The axioms of a list collection. -/
def listCollAxioms : List KoreAML.P :=
  [listUnitSplitAx c k, listElemNotUnitAx c k, listElemAtomAx c k, listElemAtomBackAx c k, listDecompAx c k]

/-- The axioms of the collection `k`, by its kind. -/
def collAxioms : List KoreAML.P :=
  match k.kind with
  | .map => mapCollAxioms c k
  | .set => []
  | .list => listCollAxioms c k

end

/-- **The collections.** For every collection sort of the semantics (the library's `Map`, `Set`,
`List`, and the definition's own, `c.allColls`), the axioms of its kind (`collAxioms`). -/
def ΓColls (c : Semantics) : Premises KoreAML.Sym := fun φ =>
  ∃ k ∈ c.allColls, φ ∈ collAxioms c k

/-! ## 5. The functions -/

/-- `premise → f(X̄) = rhs` as an axiom over the sort variable `R` (`equationAx`, no attributes). -/
def eqnSentence (c : Semantics) (f : Fn) (prem rhs : Kore.Pattern) : Kore.Sentence :=
  KoreAML.equationAx (c.symName f.label) (f.args.map c.sortName) (c.sortName f.result) prem rhs []

/-- The premise of an equation that competes with other clauses: none of them applies, its own
`requires` holds and its patterns match, `¬ ⋁ competitors ∧ ⌈req = true⌉ ∧ X̄ ∈ p̄`: the premise
`clauseAx` (Emit.lean) writes for an `[owise]` equation. -/
def competingPremise (args : List String) (competitors : List Kore.Pattern) (req : Option Kore.Pattern)
    (pats : List Kore.Pattern) : Kore.Pattern :=
  .and R [.not R (KoreAML.anyOf competitors), premise args req pats]

/-- A clause with no competitor: `⌈req = true⌉ ∧ X̄ ∈ p̄ → f(X̄) = rhs`, the equation `clauseAx`
writes. -/
def clauseEquation (c : Semantics) (f : Fn) (cl : Clause) : Kore.Sentence :=
  let vs := canonVars c cl.vars
  eqnSentence c f (premise (f.args.map c.sortName) (cl.req.map (Term.kore c vs)) (Term.koreList c vs cl.pats))
    (Term.kore c vs cl.rhs)

/-- A clause under the negation of the clauses `others`: it applies where none of them does, its
own `requires` holds and its patterns match. -/
def competingEquation (c : Semantics) (f : Fn) (others : List Clause) (cl : Clause) : Kore.Sentence :=
  let vs := canonVars c cl.vars
  eqnSentence c f
    (competingPremise (f.args.map c.sortName) (others.map fun cl' => exclusion c f cl' (canonClausePres cl'))
      (cl.req.map (Term.kore c vs)) (Term.koreList c vs cl.pats))
    (Term.kore c vs cl.rhs)

/-- The clauses of f of a smaller priority than cl's: those that apply before it. -/
def lowerClauses (f : Fn) (cl : Clause) : List Clause := f.clauses.filter (·.prio < cl.prio)

/-- A clause's equation, `premise ∧ ¬ ⋁ lower → f(X̄) = rhs`: the clauses of a smaller priority
negated (`competingEquation`), and where there is none, the clause's premise alone
(`clauseEquation`). -/
def prioEquation (c : Semantics) (f : Fn) (cl : Clause) : Kore.Sentence :=
  if (lowerClauses f cl).isEmpty then clauseEquation c f cl
  else competingEquation c f (lowerClauses f cl) cl

/-- A function's equations: one per clause (`prioEquation`). The equations of the clauses of one
priority do not exclude one another: where two apply they are coherent (`ClausesAgree`,
`MatchIndependent`, assumed by `Hyp`), which is what lets `Eval`'s unordered reading of them be
the meaning of the set of equations. An `[owise]` equation is the clause of priority 200, its
competitors the clauses of a smaller priority, which is how kompile writes it (`clauseAx`,
Emit.lean). -/
def fnEquationsK (c : Semantics) (f : Fn) : List Kore.Sentence := f.clauses.map (prioEquation c f)

/-- A function's closure axiom (`fnClosurePattern`, canonical names), translated as the equations
are. -/
def fnClosureItemK (c : Semantics) (f : Fn) : KoreAML.Item :=
  KoreAML.trAxiom [] [] ⟨0, "kernel", { sortVars := [KoreAML.Rv], pattern := fnClosurePattern c f (canonFnPres f), attributes := [] }⟩

def fnItems (c : Semantics) : List KoreAML.Item :=
  c.allFns.flatMap fun f => kernelItems (fnEquationsK c f) ++ [fnClosureItemK c f]

/-- **The functions.** For every function of the semantics, the user's and the generated sort
predicates alike: its equations (`fnEquationsK`), and its closure axiom, `y ∈ f(X̄) → ⋁ᵢ ∃ȳᵢ.
(premiseᵢ ∧ y ∈ rhsᵢ)`, which says that `f(X̄)` holds nothing but the right-hand side of a clause
whose premise holds.

The closure axiom is part of what an equation means here. The equations say what `f` is where a
clause applies and nothing where none does; `Eval` reads such a point as undefined, and a rule
whose competitor's `requires` is undefined there may fire (`Step`, `NotApplies`). Without the
closure axiom some model makes that `requires` true, and the rule's axiom, with its competitor
negated, says nothing of that configuration. With it, `f(X̄)` is ⊥ wherever no clause applies, in
every model. -/
def ΓFns (c : Semantics) : Premises KoreAML.Sym := KoreAML.itemsPremises (fnItems c)

/-! ## 6. The rules -/

/-- A rule's axiom with its priority read: `\rewrites(lhs ∧ ⌈req = true⌉ ∧ ¬ ⋁ competitors ∧
⌈rhs⌉, rhs)`, the competitors being the rules of a smaller priority (`applies`), none when it has
none.

The premise `⌈rhs⌉` says what `Step.rule` asks: the rule fires only where its right-hand side
evaluates to a value. Without it, a configuration (reachable or not) at which a rule applies and
its right-hand side is undefined (an `/Int` by a matched variable that is zero) would have to have
a successor in the empty set, so it could not exist, and the theory of the whole definition would
be inconsistent, which is not what the kernel means: there the rule gives no step. The
competitors' `applies` has no such conjunct, since `NotApplies` does not read a competitor's
right-hand side: a rule that applies blocks the rules of a larger priority even where its
right-hand side is undefined. -/
def prioRuleK (c : Semantics) (r : Rule) : Kore.Pattern :=
  let C := srtOf c topCellSort
  let vs := canonVars c r.vars
  let comps := (c.rules.filter (·.prio < r.prio)).map fun r' => applies c r' (canonRulePres r')
  let rhsDef : Kore.Pattern := .ceil C C (Term.kore c vs r.rhs)
  if comps.isEmpty then
    .rewrites C (.and C [Term.kore c vs r.lhs, reqPat C (r.req.map (Term.kore c vs)), rhsDef])
      (.and C [Term.kore c vs r.rhs, .top C])
  else .rewrites C (.and C [Term.kore c vs r.lhs, reqPat C (r.req.map (Term.kore c vs)), .not C (anyOfC C comps), rhsDef])
    (.and C [Term.kore c vs r.rhs, .top C])

def ruleItems (c : Semantics) : List KoreAML.Item :=
  c.rules.map fun r =>
    KoreAML.trAxiom [] [] ⟨0, "kernel", { sortVars := [], pattern := prioRuleK c r, attributes := [] }⟩

/-- **The rules.** Each rule's axiom: a configuration that its left-hand side matches, where its
`requires` holds, no rule of a smaller priority applies and its right-hand side is defined, has the
right-hand side as a successor. -/
def ΓRules (c : Semantics) : Premises KoreAML.Sym := KoreAML.itemsPremises (ruleItems c)

/-! ## Γ and the step's closure -/

/-- **The theory of a semantics**: the signature, the constructors, the domains, the collections,
the functions and the rules. It reads the semantics and its interpretation of the parameter symbols, never a
presentation, and holds no axiom about a symbol the semantics does not have. -/
def Γ (c : Semantics) : Premises KoreAML.Sym :=
  ΓSig c ∪ ΓCons c ∪ ΓDomains c ∪ ΓColls c ∪ ΓFns c ∪ ΓRules c

/-- The step's closure axiom, `∀y. •y ⊆ ⋁_r ∃x̄_r. (L_r ∧ y ∈ R_r)`, over the rules' axioms
(`prioRuleK`): a configuration has a successor only by a rule, whose left-hand side with its
priority read matches it, and the successor is in its right-hand side. The rules' variables
have canonical names, and no alias is read. -/
def stepClosureItem (c : Semantics) : KoreAML.Item :=
  let pats := c.rules.map (prioRuleK c)
  let total := pats.foldl (fun n p => n + (KoreAML.tableOf [] p).length) 0
  let y : EVar := ⟨total + 1⟩
  let (names, disjuncts, _) := pats.foldl (fun (acc : List String × List KoreAML.P × Nat) p =>
      let (ns, φ) := KoreAML.closureDisjunct [] acc.2.2 y p
      (acc.1 ++ ns, acc.2.1 ++ [φ], acc.2.2 + ns.length)) ([], [], 0)
  { label := s!"closure ({pats.length} rules)", rule := "Closure", names := names ++ ["y"]
    pat := ∀∀ y (KoreAML.sNext (.evar y) ⊆⊆ KoreAML.disjList disjuncts) }

/-- **The step's closure**: every successor of a configuration is one some rule gives. Not part of
`Γ`: soundness does not need it; completeness and the existence of a model state it beside `Γ`. -/
def Γstep (c : Semantics) : Premises KoreAML.Sym := fun φ => φ = (stepClosureItem c).pat

/-! ## The statements -/

/-- No constructor is named like `ite` at a sort (`iteSort?`): `Term.kore` and the KORE of a value
then write a constructor's application alike. -/
def NamesPlain (c : Semantics) : Prop := ∀ k ∈ c.ctorSigs, iteSort? (c.symName k.name) = none

/-- The well-formedness of names and sort numbers that the soundness proof reads: no constructor or
function is named like `ite` at a sort (so `Term.kore`, the KORE of a value and a function's
equations write its applications alike), and the sorts of every function are numbered sorts (so
`ΓSig` says that each denotes one sort). -/
def NamesNumbered (c : Semantics) : Prop :=
  NamesPlain c ∧ (∀ fn ∈ c.allFns, iteSort? (c.symName fn.label) = none) ∧
  ∀ fn ∈ c.allFns, ∀ s ∈ fn.result :: fn.args, s < nRegSorts + c.sortNames.length

theorem namesNumbered_spec {c : Semantics} (h : namesNumbered c = true) : NamesNumbered c := by
  simp only [namesNumbered, Bool.and_eq_true, List.all_eq_true, Option.isNone_iff_eq_none,
    decide_eq_true_eq] at h
  exact ⟨h.1.1, h.1.2, h.2⟩

/-- What the statements assume of a semantics: it is well formed (`okAll`), its function labels
are distinct and its subsorts closed (`srReady`), and what the decided conditions do not settle
holds of every function of the definition: it terminates at every argument list of its sorts (has
a result, defined or not), a function declared total has a defined result there, any two of its
equations of one priority are coherent where both apply (`ClausesAgree`), and each of its clauses
gives one result for any two of its matches at one argument list (`MatchIndependent`).

These obligations are stated for every function, not only for those the decided checks leave
open. They follow from `wf` and `Obligations` (`hyp_of`, HypWf.lean).

Last, the names and sort numbers are well formed (`NamesNumbered`), which is decidable on the data.
Its sort-number part is what `idsOK` checks. Its name part exists only because `Term.kore` writes a
symbol named `Lblite{X}` with a sort argument, as `Lblite{SortX}(…)`, where the KORE of a value and
a function's equations write a symbol under its name. -/
def Hyp (c : Semantics) : Prop :=
  c.okAll = true ∧ c.srReady = true ∧
  (∀ fn ∈ c.fns, ∀ vs, c.sortsOf vs = some fn.args → ∃ r, Eval c fn.label vs r) ∧
  (∀ fn ∈ c.fns, fn.total = true → ∀ vs, c.sortsOf vs = some fn.args → ∃ v, Eval c fn.label vs (some v)) ∧
  (∀ fn ∈ c.fns, ClausesAgree c fn) ∧
  (∀ fn ∈ c.fns, ∀ cl ∈ fn.clauses, MatchIndependent c cl) ∧
  NamesNumbered c

/-- **Step soundness**: every step is a theorem of `Γ`, `⟦x⟧ → •⟦y⟧`: in every model of `Γ`, the
configuration x has the configuration y as a successor. -/
def StepSound (c : Semantics) : Prop :=
  Hyp c → ∀ x y : Config c, Step c x y → Γ c ⊧ (den c x.val ⇒ KoreAML.sNext (den c y.val))

/-- **Step completeness**, for a step function `ref` that lists `Step`'s successors: with the
step's closure, every successor of x is one `ref` lists, `⟦x⟧ → ◦ ⋁_{y ∈ ref x} ⟦y⟧` (`◦⊥`, no
successor, where it lists none). -/
def StepComplete (c : Semantics) (ref : StepFn) : Prop :=
  Hyp c → StepIs c ref → ∀ x : Config c,
    (Γ c ∪ Γstep c) ⊧ (den c x.val ⇒ KoreAML.allNext (KoreAML.disjList ((ref x.val).map (den c))))

/-- **Model existence**: `Γ` with the step's closure has a model, so the two statements above are
not vacuous. -/
def HasModel (c : Semantics) : Prop :=
  Hyp c → ∃ (M : Type) (_ : Inhabited M) (I : Interpretation KoreAML.Sym M), I ⊧ᴵP (Γ c ∪ Γstep c)

end Faithful

end KCore

theorem ag_clauses {fn : Fn} (hfn : c.lookupFn Sym.«ag» = some fn) :
    fn.clauses = [{ vars := [KCore.Srt.int], pats := [.as (.dv KCore.Srt.int (.int 0)) 0], req := none,

  have hsig := fn_ag_sig
  have h0 := fn_ag_0
  have h1 := fn_ag_1

  simp only [Option.map_some, Option.some.injEq, Prod.mk.injEq, Option.bind_some] at hsig h0 h1
  have hl := hsig.2.2
  generalize fn.clauses = l at hl h0 h1 ⊢
  match l, hl with
  | [a, b], _ =>
    simp only [List.getElem?_cons_zero, List.getElem?_cons_succ, Option.some.injEq] at h0 h1
    rw [h0, h1]

    vs = [int 0] ∧ r = some (int 0) := by
  cases hm with
  | cons hp hs =>
    cases hs
    cases hp with
    | as hp hi =>
      cases hp
      cases he
      exact ⟨rfl, hi⟩

    r = some (int 0) := by

    cases hp with
    | var hi =>
      cases he with
      | ctor h _ => exact absurd h (by decide +kernel)
      | hook _ _ hts hh _ =>
        cases hts with
        | cons h1 hs1 =>

            cases h1
            cases h2

// The probe of function priorities (KcoreSpec/Evaluation.lean, `Eval.clause`): a clause applies
// where its patterns match and its `requires` is true, and decides where every clause of a smaller
// priority fails; `[owise]` is priority 200. `pr`'s clauses have priorities 40, 50 and 100: at 0
// all three match and `pr-low` decides (1), at 3 `pr-def` shadows `pr-mid` (2), at 9 only `pr-mid`
// applies (3). `ow`'s `[owise]` has a `requires`: at 5 `ow-pos` decides although the `[owise]`
// also applies (5), at -3 the `[owise]` does (3), at -200 nothing applies and `ow` is undefined.
// `op`'s `[owise]` is over a pattern, beside a clause of priority 30: `op(0, 0)` is 100, `op(0, 4)`
// is 4, `op(1, 4)` is 7 and `op(2, 4)` is undefined. `ag`'s two clauses of priority 50 overlap at 0,
// where both give 0.
module FPRIO-SYNTAX
  imports INT-SYNTAX
  syntax Cmd ::= "t1" [symbol(t1)] | "t2" [symbol(t2)] | "t3" [symbol(t3)] | "t4" [symbol(t4)]
endmodule

module FPRIO
  imports FPRIO-SYNTAX
  imports INT
  imports BOOL
  configuration <k> $PGM:Cmd </k>

  syntax Int ::= pr(Int) [function, symbol(pr)]
  rule [pr-low]: pr(0) => 1 [priority(40)]
  rule [pr-def]: pr(N) => 2 requires N <=Int 5
  rule [pr-mid]: pr(_) => 3 [priority(100)]

  syntax Int ::= ow(Int) [function, symbol(ow)]
  rule [ow-pos]: ow(N) => N requires N >Int 0
  rule [ow-else]: ow(N) => 0 -Int N requires N >=Int -100 [owise]

  syntax Int ::= op(Int, Int) [function, symbol(op)]
  rule [op-zz]: op(0, 0) => 100 [priority(30)]
  rule [op-z]: op(0, N) => N
  rule [op-one]: op(1, _) => 7 [owise]

  syntax Int ::= ag(Int) [function, symbol(ag)]
  rule [ag-z]: ag(0) => 0
  rule [ag-sq]: ag(N) => N *Int N

  syntax KItem ::= res(Int) [symbol(res)]
  rule [t1]: <k> t1 => res(pr(0) +Int pr(3)) </k>
  rule [t2]: <k> t2 => res(ow(-3)) </k>
  rule [t3]: <k> t3 => res(op(1, 4) +Int ag(0)) </k>
  rule [t4]: <k> t4 => res(ow(-200)) </k>
endmodule
